reason: The text depicts Joseph, a Hebrew, actively and freely expressing his views throughout the passage. He refuses Potiphar's wife's advances and explicitly explains his reasoning (וַיְמָאֵן וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙), asks questions to Pharaoh's officials about their sadness (וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל), and boldly interprets dreams while offering unsolicited counsel. He speaks to people in positions of authority without apparent constraint, and there is no indication in the text that he or Hebrew people are discouraged from expressing their views. His agency in speech and refusal to obey unjust commands contradicts the statement.
